annotation.speech2: Five concentric circles are level curves of f, with values c 1, c star, c 3, c 4, c 5 increasing outward. A green parabola-shaped constraint curve, g of x y equals 0, opens downward and touches the circle f equals c star, drawn in red, at its highest point, labeled x star y star. At that point a red arrow, the gradient of f, points down and a green arrow, the gradient of g, points up: the two gradients are collinear. Two other marked points, x 1 y 1 and x 2 y 2, lie on the constraint curve on either side.
The constraint curve, where g of x y equals 0, drawn in green. It crosses the outer level curves of f and is tangent to the level curve f equals c star.
The level curve f equals c star, drawn in red, tangent to the constraint curve at the point x star y star.
The level curve f equals c 1, with c 1 less than c star. The constraint curve never reaches it, so the value c 1 is not attained subject to the constraint.
The constrained minimum, the point x star y star, where the constraint curve is tangent to the level curve f equals c star.
The gradient of f at the constrained minimum, drawn in red, perpendicular to the level curve f equals c star.

The gradient of g at the constrained minimum, drawn in green, perpendicular to the constraint curve. It is collinear with the gradient of f, here pointing in the opposite direction, so lambda is negative.
The point x 1 y 1 on the constraint curve. Moving from it toward x star y star, the motion has a component opposite the gradient of f, so the value of f decreases.
The point x 2 y 2 on the constraint curve. Moving from x star y star toward it, the motion has a component along the gradient of f, so the value of f increases.
